definition: Condolence means an expression of sympathy in sorrow.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word condolence. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know condolence should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Neighbors she had never met left flowers and small notes of condolence on the florist's doorstep the week her husband died.
A pleasantry is far lighter than a condolence — polite small talk that acknowledges nothing graver than the weather.
Commiseration is milder than condolence — you commiserate over a lost match or a rained-out trip, while a condolence is reserved for grief.

Sympathy is the feeling of sharing another person's sorrow, and you can feel it silently. A condolence is that feeling put into words or writing — the card, the letter, the sentence spoken at the door. Sympathy lives inside; a condolence must be offered.

A consolation is anything meant to ease grief — comforting words, a kind act, a silver lining pointed out. A condolence is narrower and more formal: sympathy expressed for a loss, almost always a death. Consolation tries to make the sorrow lighter; a condolence acknowledges it.

The feeling behind it is sympathy; the condolence is what you actually say or send.
